section: Financial inclusion - PMJDY, MUDRA, microfinance and SHG-bank linkage; digital payments and UPI
subsections: PMJDY - launch, objective, features, accounts and deposits
Payment systems and NPCI products - purpose, UPI abroad

accepted.s: The National Mission for Financial Inclusion was announced on which date and formally launched on which date?
accepted.x: The National Mission for Financial Inclusion was announced on 15 August 2014 and launched on 28 August 2014.
accepted.tq: Separate announcement and launch dates instead of treating them as identical.
accepted.sec: PMJDY - launch, objective, features, accounts and deposits

accepted.s: Which institution is the nodal body for the Pradhan Mantri Jan-Dhan Yojana?
o: Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance
accepted.x: The Department of Financial Services under the Ministry of Finance is the nodal body for PMJDY.
accepted.tq: Use the institutional-authority distinction to identify the nodal body.
accepted.sec: PMJDY - launch, objective, features, accounts and deposits

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the three tenets associated with financial inclusion under PMJDY?
o: Banking the unbanked, securing the unsecured and funding the unfunded
Saving the surplus, lending to exporters and taxing households
Insuring the insured, taxing the untaxed and funding the funded
Digitising the banks, privatising the banks and regulating the markets
accepted.x: The three stated tenets are banking the unbanked, securing the unsecured and funding the unfunded.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact official wording of a three-part formulation.
accepted.sec: PMJDY - launch, objective, features, accounts and deposits

accepted.s:
With reference to PMJDY, consider the following statements:
1. Its focus shifted from every household to every unbanked adult after August 2018.
2. It forms the first layer of the JAM trinity.
3. It made Direct Benefit Transfer possible through linkage with Aadhaar and mobile services.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. PMJDY became the Jan Dhan layer of JAM, supported DBT, and shifted its coverage focus after August 2018.
accepted.tq: Verify each statement against the programme’s objective, sequence and implementation role.
accepted.sec: PMJDY - launch, objective, features, accounts and deposits

accepted.s: Which committee laid the groundwork for universal accounts, basic savings accounts and Aadhaar-linked mobile banking before the launch of PMJDY?
accepted.x: The Nachiket Mor Committee, constituted in 2013, laid the groundwork for these features of universal financial access.
accepted.tq: Match the committee with its specific reform recommendation rather than a similar banking committee.
accepted.sec: PMJDY - launch, objective, features, accounts and deposits

accepted.s:
A basic savings bank deposit account opened under PMJDY generally has which of the following features?
1. Zero minimum balance requirement
2. Interest on the balance
3. RuPay debit card
4. Provision for Direct Benefit Transfer
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: PMJDY provides zero-balance basic savings accounts with interest, RuPay debit cards and DBT functionality.
accepted.tq: Use an all-inclusive option when all listed programme features are supported.
accepted.sec: PMJDY - launch, objective, features, accounts and deposits

accepted.s: The accident insurance cover attached to the PMJDY RuPay debit card was raised to:
accepted.x: The accident insurance cover attached to the RuPay debit card was raised from ₹1 lakh to ₹2 lakh.
accepted.tq: Track the revised figure rather than the earlier amount.
accepted.sec: PMJDY - launch, objective, features, accounts and deposits

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly states the present overdraft provision associated with PMJDY accounts and the earlier amount from which it was raised?
accepted.x: The overdraft provision is up to ₹10,000, increased from ₹5,000 during Phase II of the scheme.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the revised limit from the earlier limit using paired figures.
accepted.sec: PMJDY - launch, objective, features, accounts and deposits

accepted.s: The PMJDY overdraft facility under Phase II was generally made available after which condition?
o: After one year of continuous employment
After six months of good conduct of the account
accepted.x: The overdraft facility was introduced in Phase II and could be provided after six months of satisfactory account conduct.
accepted.tq: Apply the eligibility condition to a short banking scenario.
accepted.sec: PMJDY - launch, objective, features, accounts and deposits

accepted.s: The life insurance cover of ₹30,000 under PMJDY was applicable primarily to:
o: All account holders without any condition
accepted.x: A life cover of ₹30,000 was provided for early enrollees under PMJDY.
accepted.tq: Avoid extending a limited benefit to all beneficiaries without support.
accepted.sec: PMJDY - launch, objective, features, accounts and deposits

accepted.s:
PMJDY accounts may be linked with which of the following social-security or pension schemes?
1. PMJJBY
2. PMSBY
3. Atal Pension Yojana
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: PMJDY accounts are linked with the Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana, Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana and Atal Pension Yojana.
accepted.tq: Identify the complete set of schemes linked with the account platform.
accepted.sec: PMJDY - launch, objective, features, accounts and deposits

accepted.s: As on 19 August 2026, which one of the following combinations regarding PMJDY was correct?
o: 56.04 crore total accounts and ₹2,60,859 crore deposits
59.09 crore total accounts and ₹3,16,514 crore deposits
59.09 crore total accounts and ₹2,60,859 crore deposits
45.95 crore total accounts and ₹3,16,514 crore deposits
accepted.x: As on 19 August 2026, PMJDY had 59.09 crore accounts and deposits of ₹3,16,514 crore.
accepted.tq: Pair the figures with the correct reporting date instead of mixing current and earlier data.
accepted.sec: PMJDY - launch, objective, features, accounts and deposits

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the PMJDY account position as on 19 August 2026?
o: 32.92 crore rural/semi-urban accounts and 45.95 crore women account holders
45.95 crore rural/semi-urban accounts and 14.72 crore women account holders
45.95 crore rural/semi-urban accounts and 32.92 crore women account holders
14.72 crore rural/semi-urban accounts and 32.92 crore women account holders
accepted.x: The reported figures were 45.95 crore rural/semi-urban accounts and 32.92 crore women account holders.
accepted.tq: Match each numerical indicator with its correct category.
accepted.sec: PMJDY - launch, objective, features, accounts and deposits

accepted.s: The number of PMJDY accounts in 2015 and the deposits in March 2015 were, respectively:
accepted.x: The 2015 baseline figures were 14.72 crore accounts and ₹15,670 crore deposits in March 2015.
accepted.tq: Separate account counts from deposit values and retain their respective units.
accepted.sec: PMJDY - launch, objective, features, accounts and deposits

accepted.s: Which statement regarding the reported PMJDY coverage figures in July 2026 is correct?
o: There were 32.92 crore accounts, with deposits of ₹2,60,859 crore.
There were fewer than 40 crore accounts, with deposits of about ₹1 lakh crore.
There were more than 58 crore accounts, with deposits of about ₹3 lakh crore.
There were 45.95 crore accounts, with deposits of ₹15,670 crore.
accepted.x: The July 2026 position was reported as more than 58 crore accounts and deposits of approximately ₹3 lakh crore.
accepted.tq: Use approximate wording carefully and avoid confusing subgroup figures with totals.
accepted.sec: PMJDY - launch, objective, features, accounts and deposits

accepted.s: According to the earlier reported PMJDY position dated 30 July 2025, which combination was correct?
o: 58 crore accounts and ₹3 lakh crore deposits
accepted.x: The 30 July 2025 figures were 56.04 crore accounts and ₹2,60,859 crore deposits.
accepted.tq: Use the reporting date to distinguish historical and later values.
accepted.sec: PMJDY - launch, objective, features, accounts and deposits

accepted.s: What proportion of operative PMJDY accounts was reported to be Aadhaar-seeded?
accepted.x: About 90.2% of operative PMJDY accounts were reported to be Aadhaar-seeded.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise percentage instead of substituting the broader rural or women coverage figures.
accepted.sec: PMJDY - launch, objective, features, accounts and deposits

accepted.s: The National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) is best described as:
o: A private profit-making company promoted by commercial banks alone
A Section 8 not-for-profit company promoted by RBI and the Indian Banks’ Association
A foreign payments corporation operating under the World Bank
A statutory department directly controlled by the Ministry of Finance
accepted.x: NPCI is a Section 8 not-for-profit company promoted by the Reserve Bank of India and the Indian Banks’ Association.
accepted.tq: Test the legal form and promoters together to reject institutional swaps.
accepted.sec: Payment systems and NPCI products - purpose, UPI abroad

accepted.s: NPCI functions primarily as an umbrella organisation for:
accepted.x: NPCI serves as the umbrella organisation for retail payment systems in India.
accepted.tq: Identify the core institutional function rather than an adjacent financial activity.
accepted.sec: Payment systems and NPCI products - purpose, UPI abroad

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the launch and underlying framework of UPI?
o: Launched in April 2018 with 21 banks on the RTGS framework
Launched in January 2020 with 11 banks on the NACH framework
Launched in April 2016 with 21 banks on the IMPS framework
Launched in December 2016 with 30 banks on the NEFT framework
accepted.x: UPI was launched in April 2016 with 21 banks and operated on the IMPS framework.
accepted.tq: Combine the year, participating-bank count and technological framework.
accepted.sec: Payment systems and NPCI products - purpose, UPI abroad

accepted.s:
Which of the following are characteristics of UPI?
1. It can link multiple bank accounts in one application.
2. It supports person-to-person and person-to-merchant transactions.
3. It is available round the clock.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: UPI links multiple bank accounts in one application, supports P2P and P2M payments, and operates 24x7.
accepted.tq: Check whether all statements describe the same payment platform’s functions.
accepted.sec: Payment systems and NPCI products - purpose, UPI abroad

accepted.s: Which one of the following was NOT a feature added or associated with UPI 2.0?
o: A mandatory minimum transaction value of ₹2 lakh
accepted.x: UPI 2.0 included overdraft linking, mandates, invoice checking, signed QR and a ₹2 lakh per-day limit; it did not impose a mandatory minimum transaction value.
accepted.tq: Find the option that reverses a limit into a minimum requirement.
accepted.sec: Payment systems and NPCI products - purpose, UPI abroad

accepted.s: The daily transaction limit associated with UPI 2.0 was:
accepted.x: UPI 2.0 was associated with a daily limit of ₹2 lakh.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the UPI 2.0 limit from RTGS minimum and other payment figures.
accepted.sec: Payment systems and NPCI products - purpose, UPI abroad

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: BHIM — NPCI’s UPI mobile payment application
NACH — Aadhaar biometric banking at micro-ATMs
FASTag — bulk salary and dividend payment system
accepted.x: BHIM is NPCI’s UPI mobile payment application. AePS concerns Aadhaar-enabled micro-ATM banking, NACH handles bulk repetitive payments, and FASTag is used for RFID toll payments.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure product-purpose pair and eliminate swapped functions.
accepted.sec: Payment systems and NPCI products - purpose, UPI abroad

accepted.s: AePS enables banking transactions primarily through:
o: Paper cheques processed in clearing houses
A virtual payment address without authentication
RFID tags at highway toll plazas
accepted.x: AePS enables banking at micro-ATMs using Aadhaar authentication, including biometric authentication.
accepted.tq: Match the delivery channel and authentication method with the product.
accepted.sec: Payment systems and NPCI products - purpose, UPI abroad

accepted.s: NACH is primarily used for:
o: International card acceptance at merchant terminals
Instant interbank cash withdrawal through ATMs
Bulk and repetitive electronic payments such as salaries, dividends and bills
accepted.x: NACH handles bulk, repetitive electronic payments including salaries, dividends and bills.
accepted.tq: Associate the product with its recurring-payment use case.
accepted.sec: Payment systems and NPCI products - purpose, UPI abroad

accepted.s: Which payment system is described as the largest interoperable ATM network in India?
accepted.x: The National Financial Switch, or NFS, is the largest interoperable ATM network.
accepted.tq: Use the superlative carefully and distinguish network infrastructure from payment applications.
accepted.sec: Payment systems and NPCI products - purpose, UPI abroad

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
a. IMPS — 24x7 instant interbank transfer
a. e-RUPI — person- and purpose-specific prepaid digital voucher
c. FASTag — RFID toll payment
d. 123Pay — UPI for feature phones
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. IMPS provides instant interbank transfers, e-RUPI is a targeted prepaid voucher, FASTag uses RFID for tolls and 123Pay brings UPI to feature phones.
accepted.tq: Check each product against its distinctive purpose before selecting the complete code.
accepted.sec: Payment systems and NPCI products - purpose, UPI abroad

accepted.s: BHIM, the NPCI UPI mobile application, was launched on:
accepted.x: BHIM was launched on 30 December 2016 during the post-demonetisation push.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact day and year associated with the product launch.
accepted.sec: Payment systems and NPCI products - purpose, UPI abroad

accepted.s: 123Pay is intended primarily for:
o: International remittances through credit cards only
UPI transactions through feature phones in 20 languages
accepted.x: 123Pay enables UPI services for feature-phone users and is available in 20 languages.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a feature-phone service from smartphone, ATM and toll-payment products.
accepted.sec: Payment systems and NPCI products - purpose, UPI abroad

accepted.s: e-RUPI is best described as a:
o: Person- and purpose-specific prepaid digital voucher
Universal credit card issued by NPCI
accepted.x: e-RUPI is a person- and purpose-specific prepaid digital voucher and was used in 13 government schemes.
accepted.tq: Identify the instrument by its targeted-beneficiary and purpose-specific design.
accepted.sec: Payment systems and NPCI products - purpose, UPI abroad

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the settlement mechanism of RTGS and NEFT?
o: RTGS settles in real time on a gross basis, whereas NEFT settles through deferred net half-hourly batches.
RTGS settles through deferred net batches, whereas NEFT settles individually in real time.
Both RTGS and NEFT settle only once daily on a gross basis.
Both RTGS and NEFT use identical half-hourly gross settlement.
accepted.x: RTGS settles transactions individually in real time on a gross basis, while NEFT uses deferred net settlement in half-hourly batches.
accepted.tq: Compare the two systems on settlement timing and net or gross processing.
accepted.sec: Payment systems and NPCI products - purpose, UPI abroad

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly states the minimum transaction provisions for RTGS and NEFT?
o: RTGS has no minimum, while NEFT has a ₹2 lakh minimum.
RTGS has a ₹2 lakh minimum, while NEFT has no minimum amount.
accepted.x: RTGS has a minimum transaction amount of ₹2 lakh, whereas NEFT has no minimum amount.
accepted.tq: Keep the limits attached to the correct payment system rather than reversing them.
accepted.sec: Payment systems and NPCI products - purpose, UPI abroad

accepted.s: Who operates both RTGS and NEFT in India?
accepted.x: Both RTGS and NEFT are operated by the Reserve Bank of India.
accepted.tq: Ask who performs the operational role, not who promotes retail payment companies.
accepted.sec: Payment systems and NPCI products - purpose, UPI abroad

accepted.s: Which statement about charges on RTGS and NEFT is correct?
o: Charges were replaced by a mandatory ₹2 lakh fee on both systems.
The RBI removed charges on both NEFT and RTGS.
The RBI removed charges only on NEFT.
The RBI removed charges only on RTGS.
accepted.x: The RBI removed charges on both NEFT and RTGS transactions.
accepted.tq: Reject partial statements when the stated policy applies to both systems.
accepted.sec: Payment systems and NPCI products - purpose, UPI abroad

accepted.s: Zero Merchant Discount Rate on RuPay debit transactions and BHIM-UPI was applicable from:
accepted.x: Zero MDR on RuPay debit and BHIM-UPI transactions applied from 1 January 2020.
accepted.tq: Use the exact effective date of a payment-policy measure.
accepted.sec: Payment systems and NPCI products - purpose, UPI abroad

accepted.s: The statutory basis cited for zero MDR on RuPay debit and BHIM-UPI is:
o: Section 10A of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007
Section 43A of the Information Technology Act, 2000
Section 10A of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949
Section 14 of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934
accepted.x: Zero MDR is associated with Section 10A of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the correct Act and section from nearby financial statutes.
accepted.sec: Payment systems and NPCI products - purpose, UPI abroad

accepted.s: Under the incentive scheme for small merchants, the incentive on BHIM-UPI P2M transactions up to ₹2,000 was:
accepted.x: The incentive was 0.15% for BHIM-UPI person-to-merchant transactions up to ₹2,000, with DFS as the scheme authority and NPCI as nodal body.
accepted.tq: Link the incentive percentage with the transaction ceiling and merchant category.
accepted.sec: Payment systems and NPCI products - purpose, UPI abroad

accepted.s: Which organisation serves as the nodal body for the BHIM-UPI incentive scheme?
accepted.x: The Department of Financial Services administers the incentive scheme, while NPCI is its nodal body.
accepted.tq: Separate the administering authority from the operational nodal body.
accepted.sec: Payment systems and NPCI products - purpose, UPI abroad

accepted.s: Which country was the first country to adopt UPI services abroad through NPCI International Payments Limited?
accepted.x: Bhutan was the first country listed for UPI abroad, in 2021.
accepted.tq: Identify the first country rather than a later participating country.
accepted.sec: Payment systems and NPCI products - purpose, UPI abroad

accepted.s: The UPI-PayNow linkage is associated with:
accepted.x: Singapore is associated with the UPI-PayNow linkage, which was established in 2023 after the initial 2021 connection.
accepted.tq: Use the named bilateral linkage to distinguish Singapore from other UPI partner countries.
accepted.sec: Payment systems and NPCI products - purpose, UPI abroad

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly matches countries with the years associated with UPI expansion abroad?
accepted.x: The stated sequence includes Bhutan in 2021, the UAE in 2022, Nepal in 2024 and Qatar in 2025.
accepted.tq: Start with the known country-year pairs and eliminate options with reversed chronology.
accepted.sec: Payment systems and NPCI products - purpose, UPI abroad

accepted.s: As reported for 2026, UPI had been extended to how many countries in the listed international network?
accepted.x: The reported international UPI network covered 11 countries in 2026, including Cambodia through KHQR and countries such as Greece and Maldives.
accepted.tq: Use the stated total while avoiding confusion with the number of government schemes using e-RUPI.
accepted.sec: Payment systems and NPCI products - purpose, UPI abroad

accepted.s:
Which of the following countries was included among the reported UPI international destinations in 2026?
1. Cambodia through KHQR
2. Greece
3. Maldives
4. Qatar
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Cambodia through KHQR, Greece, Maldives and Qatar were all included among the reported UPI international destinations.
accepted.tq: Test recognition of a complete country list and its special technical linkage.
accepted.sec: Payment systems and NPCI products - purpose, UPI abroad

accepted.s:
Which of the following is a feature of the newer UPI developments reported for 2026?
1. Credit Line on UPI
2. Hello! UPI
3. UPI LITE X for offline payments
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Credit Line on UPI, Hello! UPI and UPI LITE X for offline payments were listed as newer UPI features.
accepted.tq: Recognise the complete set of current product enhancements without confusing them with older UPI 2.0 features.
accepted.sec: Payment systems and NPCI products - purpose, UPI abroad

accepted.s: Which statement regarding UPI and Merchant Discount Rate is correct?
o: The amendment abolished zero MDR for all RuPay debit transactions.
UPI is charged to consumers on every transaction after the 2026 amendment.
UPI remains free for consumers, although an amendment permits a small MDR on some high-value transactions.
MDR applies only to cash withdrawals through AePS.
accepted.x: The later amendment allows a small MDR on some high-value transactions, while UPI remains free for consumers.
accepted.tq: Separate merchant-side pricing rules from consumer-facing charges.
accepted.sec: Payment systems and NPCI products - purpose, UPI abroad
